A number that is not an item is a run-time error (R003); `ListIndex = -1` chooses nothing. Items cannot be entered in the designer yet (DESIGN.md D46).
- **`ListBox.Changed`** runs whenever `ListIndex` changes: when the user picks another item, when the program sets `ListIndex` (right away, as part of the assignment, as for `TextBox.Changed`), and when `RemoveItem` or `Clear` moves or removes the chosen item, as part of that call. Removing an item above the chosen one moves the choice up by one, so the same item stays chosen; removing the chosen one, or `Clear`, leaves nothing chosen. Picking the chosen item again, or setting the same `ListIndex`, does not run it. While a ListBox's `Changed` is running, a pick in that ListBox is ignored and changes nothing (§8.1).
- **A Grid** (DESIGN.md D116) shows a table of text: a header row of column names, then rows, as a Table (§11.7) does on the form. `Cell(row, column)`, with a column's number or name, and `Header(column)` read a cell and a name and can be assigned to (`grdScores.Cell(r, "점수") = 0`); `RowCount`, `ColumnCount`, `Column`, `AddRow`, `AddColumn` and `Clear` are a Table's; `LoadCsv(path)` and `SaveCsv(path)` read and write a CSV file as `Csv.Read` and `Csv.Write` do. Rows and columns count from 0, the header not among them. `Row` and `Col` are the chosen cell (−1 when none). A click on a cell chooses it and runs `Click`; a second click on it, Enter, F2 or typing edits it (typing starts the text over), unless `ReadOnly` is `True`; Enter or a click elsewhere keeps the edit and Escape drops it. When the user has changed a cell, `Changed` runs with `Row` and `Col` on it. The program's own changes run nothing, so a `Changed` that adds the scores up and writes the total into the Grid does not start again. `ColumnWidth(column)` is a column's width in pixels: 0 at first, when the columns without a width share what the others leave, at least 96 pixels each; what does not fit scrolls. A name no column has is R032 in `Cell` and the other members; only `Column(name)` gives -1 for it. Visual Basic .NET's [DataGridView](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.forms.datagridview) and Visual Basic 6's [MSFlexGrid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa228849(v=vs.60)) are pointed to it: their `TextMatrix` is `Cell`, `Rows` `RowCount`, `Cols` `ColumnCount` (A036), and `CellValueChanged` is `Changed` (A051).
- **An Image** shows one of the project's pictures (§11.3): `imgShape.Picture = "triangle.png"` shows it, `""` shows none. The name is compared as names in code are, without case (`"Triangle.PNG"` is `triangle.png`), and reads back with the project's spelling. A name the project has no picture of stops the program (R013); written as text in the code, the analyzer warns first (A037), and in a form file it is F016. With `Stretch = False` (the default) the whole picture is fitted inside the control, keeping its proportions; with `True` it fills the control and may look squeezed. Unlike Visual Basic 6, whose Image grows or shrinks to its picture when `Stretch` is False ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa242027(v=vs.60))), the control keeps the size it was drawn at. An Image is drawn under the other controls, as a Label is (DESIGN.md D41), and takes clicks over its whole area, picture or not.
- **`Anchor`**, which every control has, names the edges of the form whose distance the control keeps when the form changes size: when the user resizes the window, or the program sets the form's `Width` or `Height` (DESIGN.md D57). It is text: `"Left Top"` (the default: the control stays where it was drawn), `"Right Bottom"` (it stays in the bottom-right corner), `"Left Right"` (it stretches with the form's width), or `""` (no edge: it stays as near the middle). The words may come in any order and case, separated by spaces or commas, and read back in the order `Left Top Right Bottom`. Anchored to two opposite edges, a control stretches, but never below 0; anchored to neither, it moves half as much as the form grows, rounded down. These are Visual Basic .NET's rules ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.forms.anchorstyles)); in Visual Basic 6 a program moves its controls itself, in `Form_Resize` ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa445540(v=vs.60))). `Left`, `Top`, `Width` and `Height` read where the control is now. A control the program places, or gives another `Anchor`, stays where it is and follows its `Anchor` from there. Text with another word stops the program (R014); written as text in the code, the analyzer warns first (A038), and in a form file it is F017.
- **`Form_Resize`** runs when the inside of the form changes size: when the user resizes the window, and when the program sets the form's `Width` or `Height` (right away, as part of the assignment, as for `TextBox.Changed`). It also runs once when the form is first shown, after `Form_Load`, as in Visual Basic 6 ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa445540(v=vs.60))). The controls have moved as their `Anchor` says by then, so the handler sees where they are and can place the others itself. A handler that sets the form's size is not started again by that change (§8.1). While a dialog is open, the form cannot be resized (DESIGN.md D58).
- **A click while a character is being composed.** Before a click reaches the program, the characters still being composed in any TextBox are committed. The order is always: the characters are committed, `TextBox.Changed` runs, then `Click` runs (or, for a click on a CheckBox or a ListBox, its `Changed`). So if the user types 한글 and clicks a button straight away, without a space, `txtName.Text` in the `Click` handler is already 한글.

### 11.2 Form files

Form `Form1` is two files side by side: `Form1.form.yaml` (the form and its controls) and `Form1.gbas` (its code). The form's name comes from the file name.

```yaml
formatVersion: 1
properties:
  Caption: Hello
  Width: 320
  Height: 120
controls:
  - name: lblMessage
    type: Label
    properties:
      Left: 16
      Top: 16
      Width: 288
  - name: btnHello
    type: Button
    properties:
      Caption: Say hello
      Left: 16
      Top: 56
      Width: 120
```

- The file is YAML, so that it is plain text (D13). The designer writes it; it can also be edited by hand, and mistakes are reported with F codes (§1.2).
- `formatVersion` is the version of this layout. A file with a newer version is not read (F003), so that an older GuBASIC never misreads it. A change that would read old files differently gets a new version and a converter (D12). A form with controls inside a Frame is written as version 2; any other form is still version 1, which version 2 reads unchanged, so that it needs no converter (DESIGN.md D105).
- A Frame's `controls` lists the controls inside it, written as the form's own (D105). Only a Frame holds controls (F021), and names are unique across the whole form.
- `menus` lists the menu bar's items (D106), each with a `name`, `properties` and, for a menu, its own `menus`; they have no `type`. A form with a menu bar is written as version 3.
- `properties` holds only the values that differ from the defaults. Keys and property names are not case-sensitive.
- Each control has a `name`, a `type` and, if needed, `properties`. A name follows the rules for identifiers (§1): an English letter, then letters, digits or `_`. It cannot be a keyword or `Form`, and two controls cannot have the same name in any case.
- A `String` property takes the value as it is written: `Caption: 2026` is the text `2026`. Use quotes for text that YAML would otherwise read differently, such as text starting with a quote, `-`, `[` or `{`, or containing `: ` or ` #`.
- The IDE always writes a form file the same way (D31): properties in the order of the component's `component.yaml`, only values that differ from the defaults, and quotes only where YAML would read the text differently (`Caption: "2026"`). Saving a form that did not change gives the same file, and Git shows only the lines that changed. Comments and the layout of a hand-written file are not kept when the IDE saves it.

### 11.3 Project files

A project is a `.gbproj` file with its forms next to it:

```yaml
formatVersion: 2
name: Shapes
startup: Form1
forms:
  - Form1
pictures:
  - triangle.png
  - circle.png
```

- `forms` lists the forms, each a pair of files as in §11.2. At least one is needed.
- `startup` is the form the program starts with; without it, the first form in `forms`. `startup: Sub Main` starts with `Sub Main` of a module (§11.5); a module cannot be `startup` (F011).
- `modules` lists the modules (§11.5), each a file `MODULE.gbas`. A name is a form's or a module's, not both (F007). A project with modules, or starting with `Sub Main`, is written as `formatVersion: 3`, which an older GuBASIC refuses to open rather than lose its modules (DESIGN.md D102).
- `pictures` lists the project's pictures, which are files in its `pictures/` folder: `pictures/triangle.png`. Only PNG, JPEG and GIF pictures are taken (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`), and a name cannot have `/ \ : * ? " < > |` (F014). Names are compared without the case of English letters, and Hangul as syllables, the same on every platform: so a project cannot have two pictures whose names differ only in case (F015), as Windows and macOS could not keep both in one folder. A project with pictures is written as `formatVersion: 2`, which an older GuBASIC refuses to open rather than lose its pictures; one without is still version 1 (DESIGN.md D51).
- `id` is the app ID (DESIGN.md D83): 8 to 32 lowercase letters and digits, made the first time the project is exported as an app and kept, so that the app exported again is the same app and keeps its settings. A copy of the project made with a new name gets a new one. One that is not an app ID is ignored (F018), and the next export makes a new one. Older GuBASICs ignore the key with F004 and drop it when they save the project.
- [examples/hello](../examples/hello) is the README example as a project.

### 11.4 Controls as objects

GuBASIC has no control arrays (DESIGN.md D95); what Visual Basic 6 did with them is done as Visual Basic .NET does it ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-studio-2008/kxt4418a(v=vs.90))): one handler for several controls (§8), and the following (DESIGN.md D98).

- **`Control`** is the type of any control on a form. Any control can be stored in it; its members are what every control has: `Name`, `Left`, `Top`, `Width`, `Height`, `Anchor` and `Tag`. A `Control` is a particular control again only through `CType` (A046). A form is not a `Control`.
- **`Name`** gives a control's name, or a form's. It can be set only on a control made with `New` that is on no form yet (A034, R019); it starts with an English letter, then letters, digits or `_` (R020).
- **`Tag`**, a `String` every control and form has, keeps any text the program wants with it, such as a number in place of a control array's index. GuBASIC does nothing with it. Written `Index`, as in Visual Basic 6, it is pointed to (A036).
- **Code written for control arrays** is told what to write instead (DESIGN.md D99): a handler taking `Index As Integer` (A049), `Command1(0)` (A050), `Load Command1(1)` and `Unload Command1(1)` (P027, P028). `On Error` says how to write `Try … Catch` (P013).
- **`Me.Controls`** (or `Form2.Controls`) are the controls on the form: in the form file's order, then in the order they were added. `Me.Controls.Count` counts them, `Me.Controls(0)` is the first, and `For Each c As Control In Me.Controls` goes through them (a snapshot: adding or removing in the loop does not disturb it).
- **`TypeOf value Is Type`** tells whether a value is a control of that type; `Nothing` is not. **`CType(value, Type)`** gives the same control as that type, and stops the program when it is another (R022); `Nothing` stays `Nothing`. Both take a control type (A045). Visual Basic .NET's `DirectCast` and `TryCast` are read as `CType` (P026).

  ```vb
  For Each c As Control In Me.Controls
      If TypeOf c Is TextBox Then
          CType(c, TextBox).Text = ""
      End If
  Next
  ```

- **`New Button`** (any control type, without arguments) makes a control on no form. Its properties start as its component's defaults and can be set at once. `Me.Controls.Add(b)` puts it on the form, on top of the others of its layer; without a `Name` it is named as the designer names one, `Button1`, `Button2`, …, by the smallest number no control of the form has or had in its form file. A name the form has stops the program (R016), as does adding a control that is on a form (R017). `Me.Controls.Remove(b)` takes a control off the form (R018 when it is not there); it keeps its name, properties and handlers, and can be added again. A form, and `Control` itself, are not made with `New` (A047).
- A control made with `New` gets its handlers with `AddHandler` (§8), not by its name. A form shown again after `Close` starts with the controls of its form file only, each with the handlers its code gives it.

  ```vb
  Dim b As New Button
  b.Caption = "No. " & count
  b.Top = 40 * count
  Me.Controls.Add(b)
  AddHandler b.Click, AddressOf Added_Click
  ```

### 11.5 Modules and `Sub Main`

A **module** (DESIGN.md D102) is code without a form, shared by the project: the file `Module1.gbas`, listed under `modules` in the project file (§11.3). File → Add Module adds one; the project explorer lists them under Modules.

- Its `Public` variables and constants, and its `Sub`s and `Function`s that are not `Private`, can be used in every form and module by their names, `Total`, or with the module's, `Module1.Total`. A name two modules make `Public` is written with its module's name (A054). A form's or module's own name of that spelling comes first.
- What it declares with `Dim` or `Private` stays its own.
- Its code cannot use `Me` or controls by themselves; it uses forms by their names: `Form1.Show`, `Form1.lblTotal.Caption`.
- Its variables get their initial values when the program starts, before the forms'.
- **`Sub Main`**: with `startup: Sub Main` (in the IDE: ⋮ next to the module, Start with Sub Main), the program starts with `Sub Main()` of a module instead of a form. It shows the forms it wants (`Form1.Show`, or `Form1.ShowDialog` to wait); when it returns, the program goes on while a form is shown, and ends when none is. `Sub Main` is in one module only (A055), and a project starting with it needs one (F019). A form's `Sub Main` is an ordinary procedure.

  ```vb
  ' Module1.gbas
  Public UserName As String

  Sub Main()
      UserName = GetSetting("user", "")
      If UserName = "" Then
          frmLogin.ShowDialog
      End If
      frmMain.Show
  End Sub
  ```

### 11.6 Files

(DESIGN.md D112, D113.) **Open and save dialogs** are `OpenFileDialog` and `SaveFileDialog`, as in Visual Basic .NET ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.forms.openfiledialog)): put on the form from the toolbox, kept in the tray as a Timer is, with `Title`, `Filter` and `FileName`. `Filter` is a label and its patterns, in pairs: `"Text files|*.txt|All files|*.*"`. `ShowDialog()` shows the dialog and waits, as a MsgBox does; it gives `DialogResult.OK`, with the file in `FileName` after the dialog's `FileOk` has run, or `DialogResult.Cancel`.

```vb
If dlgOpen.ShowDialog() = DialogResult.OK Then
    txtMemo.Text = File.ReadAllText(dlgOpen.FileName)
End If
```

**Text files** are read and written through `File`, as Visual Basic .NET's `System.IO.File` ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.file)): `File.ReadAllText(path)` gives the text; `File.ReadAllLines(path)` its lines as a `String` array, split at any line break, without an empty line after the last; `File.WriteAllText(path, text)` writes it, in place of what was there; `File.AppendAllText(path, text)` adds it at the end, making the file when there is none; `File.Exists(path)` says whether it is there. A file is read as UTF-8, with or without a byte order mark, and as code page 949, the "ANSI" text of Korean Windows in which Excel saves CSV files there, when it is not UTF-8; it is written as UTF-8, with a byte order mark for a `.csv` file so that Excel reads its Korean text. A file that is not there is R027; one that cannot be read or written R029, with what the system said. Visual Basic 6's `Open path For Input As #1` is P030.

**Line breaks and tabs** are Visual Basic .NET's constants ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/visual-basic/language-reference/constants-and-enumerations)): `vbCrLf` (carriage return and line feed), `vbLf`, `vbCr`, `vbTab`, and `vbNewLine`, which is `vbCrLf` on every platform, so that a program writes the same file everywhere.

**Where files are.** On the desktop, in the IDE and in an exported app, a path is a real one; an exported macOS app, which runs in Apple's sandbox, reaches the files the user chose in a dialog and its own folders. On the web, which has no paths, a file is known by the name of one the user chose with an `OpenFileDialog`, or one the program saved, in the same run: any other is R028. A `SaveFileDialog` there asks for the name in a dialog of the app's, and saving downloads the file under it; `File.Exists` says whether the name is one of these. Where a program runs without files (the playground), the dialogs and `File` are R030.

### 11.7 CSV files and tables

(DESIGN.md D112, D114.) `Csv.Read(path)` reads a CSV file into a **`Table`**, and `Csv.Write(path, table)` writes one, as RFC 4180 writes CSV ([RFC 4180](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4180)): cells split by commas, rows by line breaks, a cell in double quotes holding commas, line breaks and `""` for a quote. The first line is the header. Rows and columns count from 0, as a ListBox's `ListIndex` does, and the header is not among the rows.

| Member | What it is |
|---|---|
| `RowCount`, `ColumnCount` | how many rows (without the header) and columns |
| `Cell(row, column)` | a cell's text; `column` is a number or a column's name: `Cell(i, "점수")`. It can be assigned to: `t.Cell(i, "등급") = "A"` |
| `Header(column)` | a column's name; it can be assigned to |
| `Column(name)` | a column's number, or -1 when there is none |
| `AddRow()` | adds an empty row at the end and gives its number |
| `AddColumn(name)` | adds an empty column at the end |
| `Clear()` | takes away every row, keeping the columns |

```vb
Dim t As Table = Csv.Read(dlgOpen.FileName)
Dim total As Integer = 0
For i As Integer = 0 To t.RowCount - 1
    total = total + CInt(t.Cell(i, "점수"))
Next
```

A row shorter than the widest is filled with empty cells. `Dim t As New Table` makes an empty one. A file is read and written as §11.6 says: UTF-8 or code page 949 in, UTF-8 out, with a byte order mark for a `.csv` file, so that Excel opens it with its Korean text. `Csv.Write` quotes a cell that holds a comma, a quote, a line break, or space at either end, and ends each row with a carriage return and a line feed. A row or column that is not there is R031; a name no column has R032.

### 11.8 PDF files

(DESIGN.md D112, D117.) A **`PdfDocument`** is put together block by block and then saved as a PDF file:

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AddTitle(text)` | a title, in larger letters |
| `AddText(text)` | a paragraph, broken into lines to fit the page; a line break in it starts a new line |
| `AddTable(table)` | a table: a `Table` (§11.7) or a `Grid` (§11.1), as it is now |
| `NewPage()` | what follows starts on a new page |
| `Save(path)` | writes the PDF file, as `File.WriteAllText` writes (§11.6) |
| `Landscape` | `True`: the pages are on their side (D118). `False` at first |
| `TitleSize`, `TextSize`, `TableSize` | the letters' sizes in points, from 4 to 72 (R035): 18, 11 and 10 at first |

```vb
Dim pdf As New PdfDocument
pdf.AddTitle("2학기 성적표")
pdf.AddText(lblTotal.Caption)
pdf.AddTable(grdScores)
pdf.Save(dlgSave.FileName)
```

The properties apply to the whole file, as they are when `Save` runs. Pages are A4. A table is as wide as the page; its columns share it by their widest text, a cell's text wraps, and a table that goes on to another page draws its header row again there. The text is in NanumGothic, which the IDE carries; an app exported from a project whose code uses `PdfDocument` carries it too, and other apps are not made larger by it. The PDF file holds only the letters it uses. An app exported before it used `PdfDocument` has no font: `Save` is R034, and exporting it again mends it. The examples have one: **Scores** shows a list in a Grid, its total and average, and saves them as a PDF file.

### 11.9 Http and JSON

(DESIGN.md D124, D125.) **`Http`** talks to web servers, as Visual Basic 6's Internet Transfer Control did with `OpenURL` ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa733648(v=vs.60))). It is a built-in object used by its name, as `File` is, not put on a form:

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Get(url)` | the answer's text |
| `GetJson(url)` | the answer as a `Json` |
| `Post(url, body)` | sends text (`Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` unless `Header` set another) and gives the answer's text |
| `PostJson(url, json)` | sends a `Json` as `application/json` and gives the answer as a `Json` |
| `Send(method, url, body, headers…)` | sends any method (`"GET"`, `"PUT"`, `"DELETE"`, …; `""` for no body) and gives the whole answer as an **`HttpResponse`**: `Status`, `Ok` (a status below 400), `Text`, `Json` and `Header(name)`. After the body, any headers for this one request, each written `"Name: value"` |
| `Header(name)` | a header sent with every request from then on, to every server the program calls: `Http.Header("Accept-Language") = "ko"`; `""` takes it away. Not for a key, a token or a password (see **Secrets**) |
| `Timeout` | how many seconds to wait for an answer: 30 at first, from 1 to 600 |

```vb
Dim scores As Json = Http.GetJson("https://example.com/scores")
For Each s In scores
    lstScores.AddItem(s("name").AsString & ": " & s("points").AsInteger)
Next
Dim mine As New Json
mine("name") = txtName.Text
mine("points") = points
Http.PostJson("https://example.com/scores", mine)
```

**Waiting.** A call waits where it is, as `File.ReadAllText` does (§11.6), with nothing to write for it (Visual Basic .NET makes the program write `Await`: [Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/visual-basic/programming-guide/concepts/async/)): the screen keeps drawing and the Stop button works; the mouse pointer shows waiting meanwhile; clicks made meanwhile run after it, in turn (§8.1), and the same handler is not started again (D5). There is no completion event.

**Secrets.** (DESIGN.md D135.) A key, a token or a password belongs to one server. `Http.Header` is sent with every request from then on, to every server the program calls, so a secret set there goes to the others too: a weather service would receive the key of the scores service. Give it to the one request instead: `Http.Send("GET", url, "", "Authorization: Bearer " & token)` sends it with that request only, and a header named there replaces a `Header` of the same name for that request. The analyzer warns (A076) when `Http.Header` is given `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, or a name with `key`, `token`, `secret`, `password` or `auth` in it; `""`, which takes a header away, is not warned about. A header for `Send` that is not written `Name: value` is R046.

**Errors.** No answer, because the address is wrong, there is no connection, none came within `Timeout`, or on the web the server does not allow the page to call it (CORS), is R036 with what the system said; a status from 400 is R037 in all but `Send`, with the status and the start of the answer; an answer that is not JSON is R039; a header for `Send` not written `Name: value` is R046. All of them can be caught with `Try` (§9). The answer's text is read as its `Content-Type` charset says: UTF-8 when it names none, code page 949 for `euc-kr` and its other names, Latin-1 for `iso-8859-1`; bodies are sent as UTF-8.

**`Json`** is a JSON value ([RFC 8259](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259)): an object, an array, text, a number, `True` or `False`, or null. `Json.Parse(text)` reads one; `Dim j As New Json` makes an empty object and `Json.Array()` an empty array. `j("name")` is a member of an object and `j(0)` an item of an array, each a `Json` again, so `j("address")("city")` goes down a level. A value is taken out as the type it is, so that nothing is a `Variant` (§2): `AsString`, `AsInteger` (a whole number), `AsDouble` and `AsBoolean`, or `CStr`, `CInt`, `CDbl` and `CBool` of the `Json`. `Kind` says which it is: `"Object"`, `"Array"`, `"String"`, `"Number"`, `"Boolean"` or `"Null"`; `Count` is the number of members or items; `Has(name)` whether an object has a member; `Keys` an object's member names as a `String` array; `For Each item In arr` goes through an array's items. Writing: `j("name") = "Kim"` and `j("age") = 12` add or change a member (an `Integer`, `Double`, `Boolean`, `String`, `Json` or `Nothing`), `j(0) = …` changes an item, `arr.Add(value)` adds one, `Remove(name)` and `Remove(index)` take one away, and `Text` is the value as compact JSON text. Two `Json` values that share an object or an array see each other's changes, as two `List` variables do. A number read from JSON is whole when it is written whole (`12.0` is 12); one too large to be exact, `12345678901234567890`, is a `Double`. `Debug.Print(j)` and `CStr(j)` show a string's own text, a number as GuBASIC writes it (§2.2), `True` or `False`, "" for null, and an object or an array as JSON text. The wrong kind (`AsString` of a number, `j(0)` of an object, `For Each` over an object) is R040; a member that is not there R041; an item that is not there R003. A `Json` is not compared or joined with `=` or `&` (A013): take the value out first.

**Where it runs.** In the IDE and in exported apps; the playground has no `Http` (R038). Exported macOS apps may reach the network. `Http` is the first component through the component channel ([COMPONENT_CHANNEL.md](COMPONENT_CHANNEL.md)): `components/Http/component.yaml` describes it as a control's file does, and what it does is written once for the IDE and the apps. The examples have one: **Weather** shows the weather now from Open-Meteo.

### 11.10 Database

(DESIGN.md D124, D126.) **`Database`** keeps a program's data in an SQLite database ([SQLite](https://sqlite.org/)), the way Visual Basic 6 kept it in a Jet database through Data Access Objects ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa227845(v=vs.60))). It is a built-in object used by its name, as `File` and `Http` are. Every app has a database of its own, `data.db` in the app's own data folder, opened when first used:

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Execute(sql, values…)` | runs a statement and gives how many rows it changed |
| `Query(sql, values…)` | gives the rows as a `Table` (§11.7): the column names as its headers, every value as text |
| `Scalar(sql, values…)` | the first value of the first row as text; `""` when it is NULL or there is no row, and then `LastWasNull` is `True` |
| `LastWasNull` | whether the last `Scalar` found NULL, or no row |
| `LastId` | the row ID the last `INSERT` gave (SQLite's `last_insert_rowid`) |
| `Open(name)` | opens the file of that name in the app's data folder instead, making it when it is not there |
| `Close()` | closes the file; the next use opens it again |
| `Path` | where the open file is: its full path on the desktop, its name in the browser's storage on the web |
| `Export(path)` | writes the database as a file, a backup, where `File` writes files (§11.6): on the desktop at `path`, on the web as a download under that name |
| `Import(path)` | replaces the database with such a file: on the desktop the file at `path`, on the web one the user chose with `OpenFileDialog` or the program exported in this run |

```vb
Database.Execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores (name TEXT, points INTEGER)")
Database.Execute("INSERT INTO scores VALUES (?, ?)", txtName.Text, points)
Dim best As Table = Database.Query("SELECT name, points FROM scores ORDER BY points DESC")
lblCount.Caption = Database.Scalar("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scores") & " scores"
```

**Values.** A `?` in the SQL takes the next value written after the SQL, in order (SQLite's parameters: [SQLite](https://sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#varparam)): an `Integer` or a `Double` as a number, a `String` as text, a `Boolean` as 1 or 0, a `Date` as the text `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`, which SQLite's date functions read ([SQLite](https://sqlite.org/lang_datefunc.html)), and `Nothing` as NULL. Values come back as text, as a `Table` holds them: a whole number below 2⁵³ as its digits, another number as GuBASIC writes a `Double` (§2.2), NULL and a BLOB as `""`. SQL joined with `&` is a warning (A060): a quote in the value can break the statement, a `?` cannot. `Execute` without values may run several statements at once, `BEGIN; …; COMMIT;`.

**Where the file is.** On the desktop, `GuBASIC/<app ID>/` in the user's application support folder (`%APPDATA%` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS): in the IDE under the project's name, in an exported app under its app ID, so that the data an app keeps stays when the app is updated and two apps keep theirs apart. On the web, in the browser's storage (IndexedDB) under the same name, as the settings are (§10, D48); it stays as long as the browser keeps the site's data. A name given to `Open` is a file name alone, `scores.db`, not a path (R043).

**Backing up.** `Database.Export(dlgSave.FileName)` after a `SaveFileDialog` writes the whole database as one file, and `Database.Import(dlgOpen.FileName)` after an `OpenFileDialog` brings one back, on the desktop and on the web alike; the web keeps a program's database only as long as the browser keeps the site's data, so an export is its backup. A file that is not an SQLite database is R045.

**Errors.** SQL the database refuses, a mistake in it, a table that is not there or a value a column does not take, is R042 with SQLite's own words; a file that cannot be opened is R044. Both can be caught with `Try` (§9). A call waits where it is, as `Http` does (§11.9); on the web the first use loads SQLite, about 0.7 MB, and the pointer shows waiting meanwhile.

**Where it runs.** In the IDE and in exported apps, on every platform GuBASIC runs on; the playground has no `Database` (R038). The example **Notes** keeps notes in it. It is the second component through the component channel ([COMPONENT_CHANNEL.md](COMPONENT_CHANNEL.md)): `components/Database/component.yaml` describes it, and SQLite comes with package:sqlite3, the same build on every platform, so that a program's results and messages are the same everywhere. Parity programs that use it run on the VM and in the run window, and in a browser through Playwright on the built web player (`tool/web_check`).

### 11.11 WebSocket

(DESIGN.md D122, D136.) **`WebSocket`** talks to any standard WebSocket server ([RFC 6455](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455)) in text messages, today's version of what Visual Basic 6 programs did with the Winsock control ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa228119(v=vs.60))). Like a `Timer` it is not seen on the form: the designer keeps it in the tray under the form, and it is not made with `New` (A052).

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Connect(url)` | connects to `wss://…` or `ws://…` and waits until the connection is open |
| `Send(text)` | sends one text message |
| `Close()` | closes the connection; `Closed` does not run, the program knows it did |
| `State` | `"Closed"` or `"Open"` (read-only) |
| `Url` | the address last connected to (read-only); `Tag` as on every control |
| event `Message(e As MessageEventArgs)` | a message came: `e.Text`, and `e.Json`, the text read as JSON (R039 when it is not) |
| event `Closed(e As CloseEventArgs)` | the server closed the connection, or it was lost: `e.Reason` |
| event `Error(e As ErrorEventArgs)` | a problem after the connection was open: `e.Message` |

```vb
Sub Form_Load()
    wsChat.Connect("wss://relay.example.com/chat")
End Sub

Sub btnSend_Click()
    wsChat.Send(txtMessage.Text)
End Sub

Sub wsChat_Message(e As MessageEventArgs)
    lstChat.AddItem(e.Text)
End Sub
```

**Waiting.** `Connect` waits where it is, as `Http` does (§11.9): the screen keeps drawing, Stop works and the pointer shows waiting; so the line after it can `Send`. There is no `Connected` event.

**Events in turn.** Each message runs `Message` once, in the order the messages came, like a click: when the handler is running (or waits in `DoEvents`), the next message waits for it instead of being ignored, so that none is lost and the handler never runs inside itself (§8.1, D5). The events reach the form also while another form is in front, as a `Timer`'s do, and while a `MsgBox` is open they wait for it. When the form closes or the program ends, the connection is closed.

**Errors.** A connection that cannot be opened is R047, with what the system said; `Send` while the connection is not open is R049. Both can be caught with `Try` (§9). `ws://` is not encrypted, and a page served over `https` cannot open it; the analyzer warns (A077) about a `ws://` address written in `Connect` unless it is `localhost` or a private network's ([RFC 1918](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918)). Only text: a picture can go as Base64 text, and binary messages are left for later ([KNOWN_ISSUES.md](KNOWN_ISSUES.md)). Winsock's names are pointed to GuBASIC's: `SendData` is `Send` (A036), `DataArrival` is `Message` (A051).

**Where it runs.** In the IDE and in exported apps, on every platform GuBASIC runs on; the playground has no `WebSocket` (R038). It comes through the component channel ([COMPONENT_CHANNEL.md](COMPONENT_CHANNEL.md)) and is the first component with events. Parity programs talk to a scripted server, `NAME.ws`.

### 11.12 Room

(DESIGN.md D122, D136.) **`Room`** puts programs with the same room code together through a relay server: the TV's program makes a room and shows its code, the phones' programs enter it with that code, and what one sends reaches the others. Like a `WebSocket` it sits in the tray, and it speaks a published protocol ([ROOM_PROTOCOL.md](ROOM_PROTOCOL.md)), so a program not written in GuBASIC can join a room too.

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Server` | the relay server's address, `wss://relay.example.com/room`, set in the Properties window. Empty: while developing in the desktop IDE, the IDE's own relay server on this computer. A path alone, `/room`, in a web app: on the web server the app came from |
| `Nickname` | this program's nickname, which `Create` uses |
| `Create()` | makes a room and waits until it is made; then `Code` is its code and this program its host |
| `Join(code, nickname)` | enters the room with that code, in any case, and waits until it is in |
| `Send(text)` | to everyone else in the room |
| `SendTo(member, text)` | to one member |
| `Leave()` | leaves the room; when the host leaves, the room ends |
| `Lock()` | the host only: no one else may enter |
| `Code`, `Me`, `IsHost`, `Members` | the room's code, this program's member ID (`m1`, `m2`, …), whether it made the room, every member's ID as a `String` array (read-only) |
| `NicknameOf(member)` | a member's nickname |
| event `Joined(e)`, `Left(e)` | someone entered or left: `e.Member`, `e.Nickname` |
| event `Message(e)` | a message: `e.Member`, `e.Nickname`, `e.Text`, and `e.Json`, the text read as JSON |
| event `Closed(e)` | the room ended: `e.Reason` is `"host left"`, `"idle"` (nothing sent for 30 minutes), `"time"`, `"server"` or `"connection lost"` |
| event `Error(e)` | the server refused something after the program was in, a message too big or too fast: `e.Message` |

Every `e` is a **`RoomEventArgs`**; a member it does not concern is `""`.

```vb
' The TV
Sub Form_Load()
    rmQuiz.Create()
    lblCode.Caption = "Code: " & rmQuiz.Code
End Sub

Sub rmQuiz_Joined(e As RoomEventArgs)
    lstPlayers.AddItem(e.Nickname)
End Sub

Sub rmQuiz_Message(e As RoomEventArgs)
    Dim answer As Json = e.Json
    lblLast.Caption = e.Nickname & ": " & answer("choice").AsInteger
End Sub

' A phone
Sub btnJoin_Click()
    rmQuiz.Join(txtCode.Text, txtNickname.Text)
End Sub

Sub btnAnswer_Click()
    rmQuiz.Send("{""choice"":2}")
End Sub
```

**Waiting and turns.** `Create` and `Join` wait where they are called, as `Connect` does (§11.11), so the next line can read `Code`. The events run in turn, as a `WebSocket`'s do: a message that comes while `Message` runs waits for it. Messages from one member arrive in the order sent.

**A lost connection** comes back by itself within 30 seconds, keeping the program's place in the room: the others are not told, `Send` waits meanwhile, and what was sent to the program meanwhile comes after. If it cannot come back, `Closed` runs with `"connection lost"`.

**Errors.** A room that cannot be entered is R048 with the server's reason (`room-not-found`, `room-full`, `room-locked`, `server-full`, `too-fast` for too many tries); a relay server that cannot be reached is R047; `Send` while not in a room is R049. All can be caught with `Try` (§9). A `ws://` address in `Server` beyond `localhost` and a private network is warned about (A077), as for `Connect`.

**The relay server.** The relay server keeps rooms in memory only, with limits its owner can change: 50 rooms, 50 members a room, 16 KB a message, 20 messages a second a member. It is `packages/gubasic_relay`; [RELAY_SERVER.md](RELAY_SERVER.md) says how to put it on a server of your own. There is no public one: for an app others use, `Server` names your own.

**The example** **LiveQuiz** is one project for both sides: its start form asks whether this is the TV or a phone; the TV makes a room, shows its code, asks the Quiz example's seven questions and moves a runner for each player as far as its score; a phone joins with the code and answers with four buttons, `SendTo` the TV alone. In the desktop IDE it runs on the IDE's relay server; with "Allow devices on the same network" on, the Debug menu's "Preview on the Web" shows a QR code, and a phone on the same Wi-Fi opens the app from it and joins.

**Where it runs.** In the IDE and in exported apps, on every platform; the playground has no `Room` (R038). Parity programs use a relay server in memory, and their event scripts act as the others in the room: `Peer 민지 Join`, `Peer 민지 Send …`, `Room Close idle`, `Room Drop`.

## 12. Open questions

- File extension (`.gbas` is provisional).
- User-defined classes (`Class … End Class`) — not in 1.0.
- Exact syntax of the embedded-Dart escape hatch.

# Button

A button the user clicks: its Caption is the text on it, and Click runs when it is clicked.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Default event (made by a double-click): `Click`

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

| `Left` | Integer | `0` |  |
| `Top` | Integer | `0` |  |
| `Width` | Integer | `96` |  |
| `Height` | Integer | `32` |  |
| `Anchor` | String | `"Left Top"` |  |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |

- `Click()`
- `MouseDown(e As MouseEventArgs)`
- `MouseUp(e As MouseEventArgs)`

## Names other versions of BASIC use

- `CommandButton` → `Button`
- `index` → `Tag`
- `text` → `Caption`

# CheckBox

A box the user checks and unchecks, with a Caption beside it (docs/DESIGN.md D44). Changed runs after Checked changes, also when the program sets Checked (changeEvent), as TextBox.Changed does.

# ComboBox

A closed list that opens to pick one item (docs/DESIGN.md D104): Visual Basic 6's ComboBox with Style 2, the user picks and does not type. The program fills it and reads it as a ListBox (D46): AddItem, List, ListCount, ListIndex and Text, and Changed runs whenever ListIndex changes.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

| `Text` | String |  | read only |

- `RemoveItem(index As Integer)`
- `Clear()`

# Form

The form a program's controls sit on (docs/DESIGN.md §5). Width and Height are the size of the area inside the window. Resize runs when it changes, and once when the form is first shown (D58). Integer properties are 32-bit (min and max narrow that); a value outside is a run-time error (R007) or, in a form file, F012. A project's forms are shown one over another (docs/DESIGN.md D88): Show puts the form in front, ShowDialog puts it in front as a dialog and waits until it goes, Hide takes it away keeping its values, Close takes it away and starts it again the next time it is shown. Closed runs after Close.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Default event (made by a double-click): `Load`

## Properties

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Caption` | String | `""` |  |
| `Width` | Integer | `480` |  |
| `Height` | Integer | `360` |  |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |
| `KeyPreview` | Boolean | `False` |  |
| `DialogResult` | Integer | `0` | set only while the program runs |

## Methods

- `Show()`
- `ShowDialog() As Integer`
- `Hide()`
- `Close()`
- `PopupMenu(menu As Menu)`

## Events

- `Load()`
- `Resize()`
- `Closed()`
- `KeyDown(e As KeyEventArgs)`
- `KeyUp(e As KeyEventArgs)`
- `MouseDown(e As MouseEventArgs)`
- `MouseUp(e As MouseEventArgs)`

## Names other versions of BASIC use

- `text` → `Caption`

# Grid

A table of text the user reads and edits (docs/DESIGN.md D116), as Visual Basic's grids: named columns, rows and columns counted from 0, the header row not among them. A click chooses a cell (Row, Col) and runs Click; a second click on it, Enter, F2 or typing edits it unless ReadOnly, and Changed runs when the user has changed it, Row and Col on that cell. The program's own changes run nothing. LoadCsv and SaveCsv read and write it as a CSV file, as Csv.Read and Csv.Write do (D114).

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

# Menu

An item of a form's menu bar (docs/DESIGN.md D106), made in the menu editor and written under menus: in the form file. A menu with items in it opens them; an item without opens nothing and raises Click. A Caption of "-" is a line between items. Ctrl in a Shortcut is the Command key on macOS. Not seen on the form: the window draws the menu bar, or on macOS the system's menu bar does.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Default event (made by a double-click): `Click`

## Properties

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Caption` | String | `""` |  |
| `Checked` | Boolean | `False` |  |
| `Enabled` | Boolean | `True` |  |
| `Visible` | Boolean | `True` |  |
| `Shortcut` | String | `""` |  |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |

## Events

- `Click()`

## Names other versions of BASIC use

- `index` → `Tag`
- `text` → `Caption`

# OpenFileDialog

The dialog that asks for a file to open (docs/DESIGN.md D113), as Visual Basic .NET's OpenFileDialog. Not seen on the form: the designer keeps it in the tray. ShowDialog() shows it and gives DialogResult.OK with the file in FileName, after FileOk has run, or DialogResult.Cancel. Filter is "Text files|*.txt|All files|*.*": a label and its patterns, in pairs. On the web FileName is the file's name, which the File functions take in the same run; the file is read from the browser.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Not seen on the form: kept in the designer's tray.

Default event (made by a double-click): `FileOk`

## Properties

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | String | `""` |  |
| `Filter` | String | `""` |  |
| `FileName` | String | `""` |  |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |

## Methods

- `ShowDialog() As Integer`

## Events

- `FileOk()`

## Names other versions of BASIC use

- `index` → `Tag`

# OptionButton

One of a group of choices, of which one is checked (docs/DESIGN.md D104): the OptionButtons of a form are one group. Checking one, by a click or in code, unchecks the others. Changed runs when it becomes checked, as Visual Basic 6's Click did; the ones it unchecks raise nothing, so one handler for the whole group runs once.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Default event (made by a double-click): `Changed`

## Properties

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Caption` | String | `""` |  |
| `Checked` | Boolean | `False` |  |
| `Left` | Integer | `0` |  |
| `Top` | Integer | `0` |  |
| `Width` | Integer | `120` |  |
| `Height` | Integer | `32` |  |
| `Anchor` | String | `"Left Top"` |  |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |

## Events

- `Changed()`
- `MouseDown(e As MouseEventArgs)`
- `MouseUp(e As MouseEventArgs)`

## Names other versions of BASIC use

- `RadioButton` → `OptionButton`
- `index` → `Tag`
- `text` → `Caption`
- `value` → `Checked`
- `checkedchanged` → `Changed`
- `click` → `Changed`

# Room

Puts programs with the same room code together through a relay server (docs/DESIGN.md D122, D136; the protocol: docs/ROOM_PROTOCOL.md): the TV's program calls Create() and shows Code, the phones' call Join(code, nickname), and each Send reaches the others as Message. Like a Timer it is not seen on the form: the designer keeps it in the tray. Create and Join wait where they are called until the program is in the room, as Http waits (D124 A); a room that cannot be entered is R048, with the server's reason. Server is the relay server's address (wss://relay.example.com/room); empty, the desktop IDE's own relay server while developing. Send while not in a room is R049. A lost connection comes back by itself within 30 seconds, keeping the program's place; Sends meanwhile wait. Events run in turn, as a WebSocket's do; every e is a RoomEventArgs.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Not seen on the form: kept in the designer's tray.

Default event (made by a double-click): `Message`

## Properties

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Server` | String | `""` |  |
| `Nickname` | String | `""` |  |
| `Code` | String |  | read only |
| `Me` | String |  | read only |
| `IsHost` | Boolean |  | read only |
| `Members` | String() |  | read only |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |

## Methods

- `Create()`
- `Join(code As String, nickname As String)`
- `Send(text As String)`
- `SendTo(member As String, text As String)`
- `Leave()`
- `Lock()`
- `NicknameOf(member As String) As String`

## Events

- `Message(e As RoomEventArgs)`
- `Joined(e As RoomEventArgs)`
- `Left(e As RoomEventArgs)`
- `Closed(e As RoomEventArgs)`
- `Error(e As RoomEventArgs)`

# SaveFileDialog

The dialog that asks for a file to save to (docs/DESIGN.md D113), as Visual Basic .NET's SaveFileDialog. Not seen on the form: the designer keeps it in the tray. ShowDialog() shows it and gives DialogResult.OK with the file in FileName, after FileOk has run, or DialogResult.Cancel. Filter is "Text files|*.txt|All files|*.*": a label and its patterns, in pairs. On the web FileName is the file's name, which the File functions take in the same run; saving downloads the file under it.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

# TextBox

A box the user types a line of text into: its Text. Changed runs after the text changes, also when the program sets Text (changeEvent). Text holds only the characters the input method (IME) has committed, and Changed runs each time it commits one (docs/LANGUAGE.md §11.1).

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Default event (made by a double-click): `Changed`

## Properties

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | String | `""` |  |
| `Left` | Integer | `0` |  |
| `Top` | Integer | `0` |  |
| `Width` | Integer | `160` |  |
| `Height` | Integer | `32` |  |
| `Anchor` | String | `"Left Top"` |  |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |

## Events

- `Changed()`
- `MouseDown(e As MouseEventArgs)`
- `MouseUp(e As MouseEventArgs)`

## Names other versions of BASIC use

- `index` → `Tag`
- `textchanged` → `Changed`
- `change` → `Changed`

# Timer

A Timer runs its Tick every Interval milliseconds while Enabled (docs/DESIGN.md D82, D100). It is not seen on the form: the designer keeps it in a tray under the form, so it has no place or size. A tick is an event like a click: it does not re-enter, and waits while another handler runs. Start and Stop set Enabled.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Not seen on the form: kept in the designer's tray.

Default event (made by a double-click): `Tick`

## Properties

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Interval` | Integer | `100` |  |
| `Enabled` | Boolean | `False` |  |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |

## Methods

- `Start()`
- `Stop()`

## Events

- `Tick()`

## Names other versions of BASIC use

- `timer` → `Tick`

# WebSocket

Talks to any standard WebSocket server (RFC 6455) in text messages (docs/DESIGN.md D122, D136), today's version of what Visual Basic 6 programs did with the Winsock control (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa228119(v=vs.60)). Like a Timer it is not seen on the form: the designer keeps it in the tray. Connect(url) waits where it is called until the connection is open, as Http does (D124 A): the screen keeps drawing and the pointer shows waiting; a connection that cannot be opened is R047. Send(text) sends one message; while the connection is not open it is R049. Close() closes it. Message runs for each message that comes, in order, one at a time (e.Text, and e.Json read from it); Closed when the server closes the connection or it is lost (e.Reason); Error for a problem after it was open (e.Message). Through the component channel (docs/COMPONENT_CHANNEL.md): the first component with events.

Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §11](../../LANGUAGE.md).

Not seen on the form: kept in the designer's tray.

Default event (made by a double-click): `Message`

## Properties

| | Type | At first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `State` | String |  | read only |
| `Url` | String |  | read only |
| `Tag` | String | `""` |  |

## Methods

- `Connect(url As String)`
- `Send(text As String)`
- `Close()`

## Events

- `Message(e As MessageEventArgs)`
- `Closed(e As CloseEventArgs)`
- `Error(e As ErrorEventArgs)`

## Names other versions of BASIC use

- `senddata` → `Send`
- `remotehost` → `Connect`
- `dataarrival` → `Message`

# Functions

## Text

- `Len(text As String) As Integer`: The number of characters in text.
- `Left(text As String, length As Integer) As String`: The first length characters of text.
- `Right(text As String, length As Integer) As String`: The last length characters of text.
- `Mid(text As String, start As Integer, [length As Integer]) As String`: Characters of text from start (counted from 1), length of them or to the end.
- `InStr(text As String, find As String) As Integer`: Where find first comes in text, counted from 1; 0 when it does not.
- `UCase(text As String) As String`: text in capital letters.
- `LCase(text As String) As String`: text in small letters.
- `Trim(text As String) As String`: text without spaces at either end.
- `Replace(text As String, find As String, with As String) As String`: text with every find replaced by with.
- `Split(text As String, separator As String) As String()`: text cut at each separator, as an array.
- `Join(items As String(), separator As String) As String`: The items of an array joined with separator.

## Conversion

- `CInt(value As number or String) As Integer`: value as an Integer, rounding halves away from zero; text is read as a number.
- `CDbl(value As number or String) As Double`: value as a Double; text is read as a number.
- `CStr(value As any value) As String`: value as text.
- `CBool(value As number, Boolean or String) As Boolean`: value as a Boolean.
- `Val(text As String) As Double`: The number at the start of text, 0 when there is none.
- `Str(value As Integer or Double) As String`: A number as text.

## Math

- `Abs(value As Integer or Double) As Double`: The size of a number, without its sign.
- `Int(value As Double) As Integer`: The largest Integer not above value.
- `Round(value As Double, [digits As Integer]) As Double`: value rounded to digits decimals (0 when left out), halves away from zero.
- `Sqr(value As Double) As Double`: The square root.
- `Rnd() As Double`: A random Double from 0 up to, not including, 1.
- `Randomize([seed As Integer])`: Starts the random numbers again, from seed when given.
- `Min(a As Integer or Double, b As Integer or Double) As Double`: The smaller of two numbers.
- `Max(a As Integer or Double, b As Integer or Double) As Double`: The larger of two numbers.

## Arrays

- `UBound(items As array) As Integer`: The largest index of an array.

## Date and time

- `Now() As Date`: The date and time now, on this device.
- `Today() As Date`: Today's date, at midnight.
- `Year(date As Date) As Integer`: The year of a date.
- `Month(date As Date) As Integer`: The month of a date, 1 to 12.
- `Day(date As Date) As Integer`: The day of a date.
- `Hour(date As Date) As Integer`: The hour of a date, 0 to 23.
- `Minute(date As Date) As Integer`: The minute of a date.
- `Second(date As Date) As Integer`: The second of a date.
- `DateAdd(interval As String, number As Integer, date As Date) As Date`: date with number intervals added: "yyyy", "q", "m", "d", "ww", "h", "n", "s", or DateInterval.
- `DateDiff(interval As String, date1 As Date, date2 As Date) As Integer`: How many intervals from date1 to date2.
- `Format(value As any value, format As String) As String`: A date or a number written with a .NET format string: custom ("yyyy-MM-dd", "#,##0") or standard ("d", "N2", "C").

## Dialogs

- `MsgBox(prompt As String, [title As String])`: Shows a message and waits for OK.
- `InputBox(prompt As String, [title As String], [default As String]) As String`: Asks for a line of text; "" when cancelled.

## Program

- `DoEvents()`: Lets the screen draw and other events run, then goes on.

## Settings

- `SaveSetting(key As String, value As String)`: Keeps a value under key for this app.
- `GetSetting(key As String, default As String) As String`: The value kept under key, or default.

### Database

Keeps a program's data in an SQLite database file (docs/DESIGN.md D124, D126), the way Visual Basic 6 kept it in a Jet database through Data Access Objects (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa227845(v=vs.60)). A built-in object used by its name, not put on a form. Every app has a database of its own, data.db in the app's own data folder, opened when first used; Database.Open(name) opens another file there instead. Execute(sql, values…) runs a statement and gives how many rows it changed; Query(sql, values…) gives the rows as a Table; Scalar(sql, values…) gives the first value of the first row as text, "" for NULL or no row, and LastWasNull says which. A value goes into the SQL as a ?, and after it in the call: Database.Execute("INSERT INTO scores(name, points) VALUES (?, ?)", txtName.Text, points); a quote in the value then cannot break the statement. Integer, Double and String go in as they are, Boolean as 1 or 0, Date as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", Nothing as NULL. LastId is the row ID the last INSERT gave; Path is where the file is; Close() closes it (the next use opens it again). Export(path) writes the database as a file, a backup, where File writes files (on the web, a download); Import(path) replaces the database with such a file, one chosen with OpenFileDialog or exported in this run on the web. SQL the database cannot run is R042; a name that is not a file name is R043; a database that cannot be opened is R044; a file that is not an SQLite database is R045. SQL joined with & is a warning (A060).

- `Database.Path As String`
- `Database.LastWasNull As Boolean`
- `Database.LastId As Integer`
- `Database.Open(name As String)`
- `Database.Execute(sql As String, ParamArray values As number, Boolean, String, Date or Nothing) As Integer`
- `Database.Query(sql As String, ParamArray values As number, Boolean, String, Date or Nothing) As Table`
- `Database.Scalar(sql As String, ParamArray values As number, Boolean, String, Date or Nothing) As String`
- `Database.Close()`
- `Database.Export(path As String)`
- `Database.Import(path As String)`

### Http

Talks to web servers over HTTP (docs/DESIGN.md D124, D125), the way Visual Basic 6's Internet Transfer Control did with OpenURL (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/aa733648(v=vs.60)). A built-in object used by its name, not put on a form: Http.Get(url) gives the answer's text, Http.GetJson(url) its JSON, Http.Post(url, body) and Http.PostJson(url, json) send a body and give the answer, and Http.Send(method, url, body) gives the whole answer as an HttpResponse, whatever its status. A call waits where it is, as File.ReadAllText does: the screen keeps drawing, the pointer shows waiting, and clicks made meanwhile run after it, in turn. Header(name) is a header sent with every request from then on, to every server the program calls ("" takes it away), so a key, a token or a password does not belong there (A076): Send takes, after the body, headers for that one request, each written "Name: value", and one named there replaces a Header of the same name for that request (D135). Timeout is how many seconds to wait for an answer. A request that gets no answer is R036; a status from 400 is R037 in all but Send; text that is not JSON is R039; a header for Send that is not written "Name: value" is R046. The first component through the component channel (docs/COMPONENT_CHANNEL.md).

- `Http.Timeout As Integer (can be set)`
- `Http.Get(url As String) As String`
- `Http.Post(url As String, body As String) As String`
- `Http.GetJson(url As String) As Json`
- `Http.PostJson(url As String, body As Json) As Json`
- `Http.Send(method As String, url As String, body As String, ParamArray headers As String) As HttpResponse`
- `Http.Header(name As String) As String (can be assigned to)`

## Structures

A program's own types: `Structure Student … End Structure`, fields only,
in a module for the whole project or in a form for that form.
Explained in [LANGUAGE.md §4.1](../LANGUAGE.md).

- A Structure is copied when it is stored (assigned, passed, returned, put
  into an array or a List), **its array fields too**. A plain array
  assigned to another variable (`y = x`) is **the same array**.
- A field is changed where the value is: `list(0).Score = 95` changes the
  item of a `List(Of Student)`. Visual Basic .NET refuses this (BC30068).
- For Each gives copies (A066). Not done with a Structure: comparing it
  (A063), text (A064), `Object` (A067).
- A value in one expression: `New Student With {.Name = "Kim", .Score = 90}`.
  Lists of items for arrays: `.Choices = {"a", "b", "c", "d"}`,
  `Dim names() As String = {"Kim", "Lee"}`, `Total({4, 5, 6})`. Inside the
  braces a line may break without `_` (LANGUAGE §1, §4).

## Constants

- `vbCrLf`: `\r\n`
- `vbNewLine`: `\r\n`
- `vbLf`: `\n`
- `vbCr`: `\r`
- `vbTab`: `\t`
